messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**標準誤（Standard Error）**

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

其中  
- \(s = 1.4\)（樣本標準差）  
- \(n = 40\)（樣本大小）

計算：

\[
SE = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

因此，對於零假設檢定，樣本平均值的標準誤（即「標準差」）約為 **0.22**。
message.reasoning:
The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test? Actually they say "零假設檢定的標準差" which might mean "standard error" or "standard deviation of the sampling distribution"? They provide sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, population mean 98.6. They want to compute something. Possibly they want the standard error of the mean: SE = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under null hypothesis? That is same as SE. So answer: 0.2215.

But maybe they want to compute the t-statistic? They didn't ask for p-value. They asked "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" That is ambiguous. They might want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean (i.e., standard error). So answer: 0.2215.

Alternatively, they might want to compute the standard deviation of the null hypothesis distribution? That is the population standard deviation? But we don't have that. So likely they want the standard error.

Thus answer: 0.2215.

We can also mention the formula: SE = s / sqrt(n). So 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.2215.

Thus answer: 0.2215.
